title: KPI Signal Synthesis and Ownership Matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc synthesizes the launch KPIs we will track for the X-stage rollout, maps each signal to an accountable owner, and captures decision protocols (go/no-go triggers, mitigation steps). Intention: produce a compact operational reference for launch day + first 7 days and for post-launch retros.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Primary launch objective: stable user-facing latency < 350ms median for 95% of requests while keeping per-token cost within target budget band.
- Focus signals: latency p95/p99, error-rate (5xx + client timeouts), quota overage events, cost per 1k tokens, new user activation conversion, and key quality regressions (eval prompt set).
- Owners assigned; escalation ladder defined; immediate mitigations enumerated.

KPI heatmap and thresholds (operationalized):
1) API latency (generation path)
   - Metric: median, p95, p99 (ms) by route and model variant
   - Target (green): median < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms
   - Warning (amber): p95 300-500ms or p99 700-1200ms
   - Critical (red): p95 > 500ms or p99 > 1200ms
   - Trigger: 3 consecutive 5-minute windows in amber -> paging to SRE/product-ops; critical -> immediate traffic reduction to fallback model(s) and auto-scale request.

2) Error rate (5xx + gateway timeouts)
   - Metric: errors / total requests, 1m and 1h windows
   - Target: < 0.2% (1h)
   - Warning: 0.2% - 1%
   - Critical: > 1% or any spike > 5% in 1m
   - Trigger: >1% sustained for 10m -> canary abort and rollback routing changes; >5% -> emergency rollback / serve-from-cache policy.

3) Cost per 1k tokens (hosted/dedicated split)
   - Metric: $ per 1k gen tokens (moving 24h avg)
   - Target: <= $0.65 / 1k (hosted) / <= $0.40 (dedicated)
   - Warning: +10% above target
   - Critical: +25% above target -> throttle non-critical routes and enable batching/caching profile recommended by Optimize.

4) Quality regression signal (eval suite)
   - Metric: pct change in eval pass-rate on canary prompt set (weighted)
   - Target: no negative delta > 1.5% average across critical prompts
   - Trigger: drop >1.5% -> pause rollout and run targeted model diff evaluation; if confirmed, rollback to previous model.

Ownership matrix (who does what):
- Product-ops lead: Maya Chen (owner of readiness doc, overall decision authority for non-SRE rollbacks)
- SRE on-call: Noah Kim (infrastructure health, scaling, incident response)
- Serving runtime lead: Jordan Patel (model variant routing, kernel fallbacks, quantization toggles)
- Customer success escalation: Priya Rao (customer comms, priority support lanes)
- Observability & telemetry: Eleanor Brooks (dashboards, alert tuning, postmortem notes)

Quick ownership table (text representation):
Signal | Primary owner | Backup | Pager? | Immediate action
API latency | Jordan Patel | Noah Kim | yes | scale, reduce batch size, route to fallback model
Error rate | Noah Kim | Jordan Patel | yes | abort canary, rollback routing, enable circuit breaker
Cost per 1k | Maya Chen | Jordan Patel | no | enable aggressive batching, turn on cache TTL reduction
Quality regressions | Maya Chen | Eleanor Brooks | no | pause rollout, run differential eval, notify PM/Research
Customer escalations | Priya Rao | Maya Chen | no | triage ticket, provide mitigation ETA

Decision protocols (short actionable rules):
- Canary stop: any single critical signal (red) observed for 5 continuous minutes -> stop traffic to canary and notify product-ops + SRE.
- Auto-fallback: if latency p95 > 500ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute checks AND error-rate rising -> route 30% traffic to cheaper variant, evaluate cost/quality tradeoff.
- Throttle policy: cost critical -> reduce non-essential analytic routes to 10% traffic, switch batcher to compact mode.

First 72 hours runbook (minute-to-hourly cadence):
- T-minus 0 (pre-traffic): verify dashboard sanity, smoke test 10 staged requests per route, confirm canary metric baselines.
- Hour 0-1: monitor 1m granularity for latency and errors. Check top-5 stack traces.
- Hour 1-6: shift to 5m granularity. Confirm cost delta < 10% expected.
- Hour 6-24: monitor 15m windows for anomalies; daily debrief at +12h and +24h.
- Day 2-3: focus on quality regressions from rational sample; reconcile any customer reports.

Staffing and escalation (rotas):
- Launch commander (primary contact): Maya Chen (first 48h), handoff to product-ops on-call afterwards.
- SRE rota: Noah Kim (launch), backup: Alex Rivera (SRE #2) — add to PagerDuty schedule (ticket: PRODOPS-812).
- Observability support: Eleanor Brooks will own dashboard tweaks and immediate alert threshold changes.
- Communication channel: #launch-x-stage (Slack) and "Launch Command" Google doc for minute-by-minute notes.

Monitoring queries & dashboards (notes / copy for Eleanor):
- latency_by_route: SELECT route, PERCENTILE(lat_ms, 50, 95, 99) FROM requests WHERE env = 'prod' AND window=5m
- errors_by_code: GROUP BY status_code, route -> heatmap at 1m
- cost_token_rate: movingAvg(cost / tokens, 1h)
- quality_eval_delta: compare canary eval to baseline, weighted by prompt traffic share

Known risk and mitigations (short list):
- Risk: sudden spike in small prompt chat usage causes KV cache thrash -> Mitigation: lock prefix caching TTL, apply hot-key routing to dedicated pool.
- Risk: quantized variant produces rare hallucination on finance prompts -> Mitigation: route finance customers to higher-fidelity model variant and add post-filter check for hallucination triggers.
- Risk: quota bursts from test accounts -> Mitigation: enforce per-account rate limits, temporarily suspend test tenants.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed: (notes to self)
- Who is authorized to flip the global fallback switch outside SRE? (need org decision; propose Maya + Noah joint auth)
- Runbook: should we auto-scale up Dedicated pool beyond reserved during launch hour-1? cost tradeoff needs approval from finance.
- Confirm which exact eval prompt set is the canonical canary set (current candidate: eval/launch-x-v2.json in research repo).

Next actions (owners + due dates):
- Finalize alert thresholds and create PagerDuty escalation: Noah Kim (due 2026-02-24)
- Build the canary dashboard tile + annotate thresholds: Eleanor Brooks (due 2026-02-22)
- Validate billing forecast under 2x traffic: Maya Chen + Finance (due 2026-02-25)
- Freeze model variant set and publish rollout manifest: Jordan Patel (due 2026-02-23)

Appendix (notes & links):
- Slack thread: https://slack-redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123LAUNCH for pre-launch chatter
- Research canary repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/main/canary/launch-x
- Linear tickets referenced: LNR-3345 (dashboard), LNR-3370 (canary tests)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first 2 hours conservative. If anything smells off, reduce traffic and run postmortem on that window rather than pushing forward.
- Don't let cost panic override quality checks; customers notice regressions faster than we regain trust.
